name: Discord
verdict: Better than most social platforms on privacy, but growing ad ambitions and broad content rights warrant attention.

analysis.verdict: Better than most social platforms on privacy, but growing ad ambitions and broad content rights warrant attention.

whatTheyCollect.details: All messages, voice/video call metadata, file uploads, and reactions. Messages are stored on Discord's servers, not end-to-end encrypted.
Which servers you join, channels you visit, games you play, Spotify listening activity, and online/idle/DND status.
IP address, device identifiers, OS, browser type, and referring URLs.
For Nitro subscribers: billing address, payment method details processed via third-party payment processors.
Date of birth, and in some regions, government ID for age verification required to access age-gated content.

whatTheyDoWithData.details: Messages stored to deliver them across devices. Unlike some platforms, Discord has historically not sold message data for advertising.
Discord introduced Sponsored Quests and is building an ad platform. User engagement data will increasingly drive ad targeting.
Content is scanned for child safety violations, spam, and terms violations. Reports trigger human review of messages.
Usage patterns analyzed to improve features, including which server features are used most and engagement metrics.

rightsYouGiveUp.title: Content License
rightsYouGiveUp.originalText: By uploading, distributing, transmitting or otherwise using Your Content with the services, you grant to us a nonexclusive, transferable, royalty-free, sublicensable, and worldwide license to use, store, display, reproduce, save, modify, create derivative works, perform, and distribute Your Content.
rightsYouGiveUp.translation: Standard broad license. Discord can use your messages, images, and uploads for service operation and potentially more. Transferable and sublicensable means third parties could access it.

rightsYouGiveUp.title: Binding Arbitration
rightsYouGiveUp.originalText: You and Discord agree that any dispute, claim, or controversy will be settled by binding arbitration.
rightsYouGiveUp.translation: No class actions or jury trials. Standard tech company arbitration clause.

rightsYouGiveUp.title: Terms Modification
rightsYouGiveUp.originalText: We may update these terms. We'll notify you of material changes.
rightsYouGiveUp.translation: Discord can change terms with notice. They do provide notification but continued use equals acceptance.

howToLeave.canDelete: Yes — account deletion available through Settings. Data is queued for deletion within 14-30 days.
howToLeave.dataRetention: Messages in servers persist after account deletion (shown as 'Deleted User'). DMs are deleted.
howToLeave.dataPortability: Request Your Data feature available. Returns account info, messages, and activity data.

redFlags.whyItMatters: All messages are readable by Discord in plaintext. This means staff, moderators with access, or law enforcement with a subpoena can read everything.
redFlags.industryComparison: Signal and WhatsApp offer E2E encryption by default. Telegram offers it optionally. Discord's lack of encryption is a notable gap for a messaging platform.

redFlags.whyItMatters: Discord's shift toward ads (Sponsored Quests, in-app promotions) signals that user engagement data will increasingly be monetized.
redFlags.industryComparison: Discord is following the path that Facebook and Instagram took — starting ad-free, then gradually introducing advertising as the primary revenue model.

redFlags.whyItMatters: Even after deleting your account, messages you sent in servers remain visible (attributed to 'Deleted User'). Years of conversations persist without your control.
redFlags.industryComparison: Most messaging platforms delete messages when accounts are deleted. Discord's approach is more like a forum where posts outlive the poster.

analysis.bottomLine: Discord is currently better than average on privacy — no message-based ad targeting yet, decent deletion timeline, and transparent about data use. But the trajectory is concerning: no encryption, growing ad platform, and server messages that outlive your account. If you use Discord for sensitive conversations, know that nothing is encrypted and everything persists. The platform is mid-transition from privacy-respectable to ad-supported.
